findings.title: Attacks 21 and 22: the T12 string viewer's node hit areas are below the 6.1 rule at 320 px (39 instead of 43, 34 instead of 38) and on eight-column boards at 360 px, because the panel, not the edge-to-edge figure, is the board's size container
findings.location: site/src/components/tools/T12RepresentationBuilder.svelte:1209-1218 (.panel { container-type: inline-size; padding: 8px 12px; border: 1px }), with site/src/components/board/Board.svelte:217 and :227 (--u: min(64px, (100cqw - 16px) / k))
findings.claim: Board.svelte computes u from the nearest inline-size container. T12 makes each .panel such a container, so on /tools/rep/ u is computed from the panel's content box (W - 26), not from the figure, which runs from edge to edge below 400 px. Every board with seven or eight columns gets hit areas smaller than SPEC 6.1 and A-7 require.
findings.expected: SPEC 6.1: u = min(64, floor((W - 16)/k)) with W the viewport width below 400 px, and a hit side of min(44, u). A-7: '43 for seven (E8), 38 for eight'. So 43 on A7, B7, C7, D8 and E8 at 320, 38 on A8, B8 and C8 at 320, and 43 on A8, B8 and C8 at 360.
findings.observed: /tools/rep/ at 320x800: every node button on ?g=E8&k=8, ?g=D8&k=1 and ?g=A7&k=1 is 39x39, and on ?g=A8&k=1 and ?g=B8&k=1 it is 34x34. At 360x800, ?g=A8&k=1 is 39x39. The board group is 273 px wide inside a 320 px figure. T12.spec.ts 'at 320 pixels ... targets are large enough' checks only >= 24, so it passes. P5-A2-review recorded the 39 and 34 px in its notes; this was not repaired.
findings.reproduction: From a clean checkout of 006f50d plus the reproducer: npm ci; npm run build; then npx playwright test redteam-RT-05-p5-t12-hit-side. Here: PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH=<scratch>/pw-browsers npx playwright test -c <scratch copy of playwright.config.ts on port 5350> redteam-RT-05-p5-t12-hit-side. Result: 6/6 fail with 'node 1 hit area 39 x 39, expected 43 x 43' and similar.
findings.specRef: SPEC.md 6.1 'Size on screen' ('On a viewport narrower than 400 pixels the box runs from edge to edge of the viewport, so W is the viewport width'); 7.5 A-7; 8.1 P11; CONTRACTS 5.1 'Hit area min(44, u) per 6.1'
findings.proposedFix: Do not make the string panel the board's inline-size container. For example, move container-type from .panel to the .matrices wrapper that needs it, or give .board-host its own container that runs edge to edge (negative inline margins equal to the panel's padding and border below 400 px). Tighten T12.spec.ts to the 6.1 values.

findings.title: Attack 2: when a T12 island hydrates, the server's matrix and relation scroll boxes are replaced, so a keyboard reader whose focus is on one of them is thrown to <body> (M8 b4's first tab stop)
findings.location: site/src/components/tools/T12RepresentationBuilder.svelte:456-474 (goLive) and :488-514 (activate), which replace the server markup of the relations, matrices and string panels; site/src/components/math/MatrixView.svelte:283-288 and :294 (adopt moves only the <table> into a new .box; the server's .box tab stop is discarded)
findings.claim: Before hydration, the server markup of T12 holds scroll boxes (tabindex=0, role=group) for E, F, H and the two sides of the relation. They are the tool's only enabled tab stops, because the selects are disabled until hydration. After hydration, activate swaps those panels for live ones and the focused box is removed. On M8 every island after b1 is client:visible, so tabbing onto such a box is what makes the island hydrate, and the focus is then lost.
findings.expected: 7.5 A-1 'Every tool is fully operable from the keyboard' and WCAG 2.4.3: the focus stays on the box the reader is on, or on its live replacement, as for every other control since the P3-RT-05-09 and P4-RT-05-01 fixes.
findings.observed: M8 b4 (preset relation-checker): with the focus on the server box 'Left side', which is one Tab from the prose before b4, document.activeElement becomes BODY once data-hydrated=true and data-drawn=true. The same happens on b3 with the box E1. The focus survives on the orbit box and the signed box, whose panels are not swapped. 6/6 runs fail at load averages 2 to 24.
findings.reproduction: From a clean checkout of 006f50d plus the reproducer: npm ci; npm run build; then npx playwright test redteam-RT-05-p5-t12-focus-at-hydration (here with the scratch config on port 5350 and PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH set). The test focuses the box without scrolling, then scrolls it into view, which is what a Tab does, in two steps so that hydration cannot start first. Result: 'Expected: div in b4 (relation-left), Received: BODY', and the same for b3 matrix-e.
findings.specRef: SPEC.md 7.5 A-1 and A-2 (target WCAG 2.2 AA, 2.4.3 Focus Order); 4.0 'Keyboard and screen reader'; the precedents P3-RT-05-09 and P4-RT-05-01
findings.proposedFix: Adopt the server's scroll box itself instead of only its table: let MatrixView take over the adopt root's .box, keep its focus and update its caption id. Alternatively, in goLive, record the focused element's data-out inside the replaced panel and focus the matching live box after the swap.

findings.title: Attacks 1 and 16: a relation verdict computed in the worker is drawn but never announced; the live region says only 'checked in the background'
findings.location: site/src/components/tools/T12RepresentationBuilder.svelte:612-631 (acceptFromWorker draws the sides, the verdict and the count, and moves to failingDefault, without announcing); site/src/components/tools/t12/model.ts:625-630 (relationSentence with check === null)
findings.claim: Where the relation list goes to the worker (E6 nodes 1 and 6, E7 node 7, every rank-8 list, and any configured state whose digest does not hold the picked relation), picking a relation announces '<formula>: checked in the background.'. When the list arrives, the verdict 'equal' or 'not equal' and the count of relations that hold appear with no announcement. A screen-reader reader never hears the result of the check. Also silent: the jump to the first failing relation on C5 to C8 node n, and the 'not checked' state after a worker failure.
findings.expected: 4.0 'a polite live region announces each result with the wording fixed in section 7.5'; 7.5 A-4 and WCAG 4.1.3 Status Messages. When the verdict appears, the region says it, for example '[H1, F1] = ...: the two sides are equal.'.
findings.observed: M8 b6 (E6, node 1), relation select ArrowUp: the screen shows the verdict 'equal' (data-holds=true), while the live region said only '[H1, F1] = −2F1: checked in the background.'. M8 b7 (E7, node 7): screen 'equal', region only '[H7, F7] = −2F7: checked in the background.'.
findings.reproduction: From a clean checkout of 006f50d plus the reproducer: npm ci; npm run build; then npx playwright test redteam-RT-05-p5-t12-verdict-unannounced (here with the scratch config on port 5350). Result: 2/2 fail with the messages above.
findings.specRef: SPEC.md 4.0 'Keyboard and screen reader'; 7.5 A-4 (criterion 4.1.3) and the WCAG 2.2 AA target
findings.proposedFix: In acceptFromWorker, when the list belongs to the representation shown, announce relationSentence(tool, shownCheck(...)) through the frame's announce (and the moved relation when failingDefault applies), as pickRelation does when the list is on the main thread. Announce the 'not checked' state as well.

findings.title: Attacks 1 and 36 (plan wording): T12's relation and pick announcements read the visual formula, with U+2212 and a caret exponent, instead of the spoken form T12 gives the same formula
findings.location: site/src/components/tools/t12/model.ts:619-630 (pickSentence, relationSentence); site/src/components/tools/t12/rep.ts:593-605 and :622-625 (sideText and relationText, against relationSpoken at :628-631); rep.ts:433 (explanation)
findings.claim: The live-region sentences after a relation pick and a node pick are built from display text: '[H1, F1] = −2F1', 'ad(E1)^2 E2 = 0', 'every number in the orbit of ω2 is −1, 0 or 1'. The formula on the page is named in words by relationSpoken ('H 1 F 1 commutator equals minus 2 F 1', 'ad E 1 to the power 2 applied to E 2 equals 0'). A screen reader therefore hears a caret, or loses the exponent, and gets the symbol U+2212 where every A-4 template says 'minus'.
findings.expected: A-4 'with negative numbers spoken as minus', which the build applies through speak in every move template, and A-12. The announcement should use relationSpoken and speak.
findings.observed: /tools/rep/ (A2): ArrowUp on the relation select announces '[H1, F1] = −2F1: the two sides are equal.'; ArrowDown announces 'ad(E1)^2 E2 = 0: the two sides are equal.'; ArrowDown on the node select announces 'A2, node 2: the orbit of ω2 has 3 positions. Node 2 is minuscule: every number in the orbit of ω2 is −1, 0 or 1, and all the relations hold.'
findings.reproduction: From a clean checkout of 006f50d plus the reproducer: npm ci; npm run build; then npx playwright test redteam-RT-05-p5-t12-relation-announcement (here with the scratch config on port 5350). Result: 3/3 fail.
findings.specRef: SPEC.md 7.5 A-4 and A-12; CONTRACTS 4 speak. The sentences are plan readings (decisions/P5-A2.md), so this is minor.
findings.proposedFix: Build relationSentence from relationSpoken, and write the explanation in pickSentence with speak (or 'minus 1, 0 or 1').

notes: Test strength: T12.spec.ts 'at 320 pixels ... targets are large enough' asserts only >= 24, so it cannot catch P5-RT-05-01. lesson-reflow.spec.ts lists M0 to M5 only, not M6, M7 or M8. M8 has no page scroll at 320 in my runs, so this is a coverage note for the owner, not a finding.

Page.astro's scoped '.table-wrap:focus-visible' rule does not reach the MDX tables of /not-quiver-mutation/ and of the M8 sidebar (role=region, tabindex=0), so they show Chromium's default focus ring instead of the site's 3px --focus-ring. The default ring is visible, so this is a consistency note, not an A-2 finding.

Long values in T12's string line: the exact digits of the line's other end, for example (-12345678901234567890, 12345678901234567891), are only in the item's title, which Chromium exposes as the listitem's name (with an ASCII hyphen), in data-value and in Download data. The table view lists the board's values but not the line. This is a borderline reading of 4.0 'Long numbers' after last round's refutation of P4-RT-05-04, and is left as a note.

Plan readings seen, consistent with recorded readings: Reset announces 'Undid move 1. Numbers now ...' as T1 does. PageDown on the slider jumps 5 positions and announces 'Undid move 46. Numbers now ...'. The pick sentence names ω1 rather than 'omega 1'.
M8 has four page-level polite status regions outside the tools: the Challenge components, empty at load, as on earlier lessons.

Environment: a load average of up to 24 late in the run, from other agents. My first, keyboard-only version of the focus reproducer raced hydration once under that load, so the committed version separates focus and scroll to stay deterministic (6/6 fail). My long-running preview server on 5350 and release server on 5351 were stopped by the harness's background time limit; Playwright's webServer restarted the preview as needed. No other agent's ports were touched.

Not rerun this round because their code is untouched since gate-G3 or gate-G4: the full arrow table, node centres, custom @ fallback, road styles, polygon radius, the mutation pass over the gate's keyboard scripts, and keyboard-only T2 and T8. T13 and embeds are phase 6.
